SMTO-UI-0029 — The Settings page didn't load completely

GUID: 8681f866-f949-4da4-9f0f-04be52d1b213
Slug: ui-shared-component-unavailable
Domain: UI · Subsystem: ui

What happened

  • Part of the Settings page didn't download, so it can't load or save your settings right now. Your saved settings haven't been changed.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Reload the Settings page (press Ctrl+Shift+R, or Cmd+Shift+R on a Mac). A full reload downloads every part of the page again, which fixes a part that failed to load once.
  2. Make sure you are still connected to the network and that the SMTO main page opens in another tab. If the connection to SMTO dropped, the browser couldn't download the missing part of the page.
  3. If SMTO was updated recently, close every SMTO tab, then open SMTO again. A tab left open from before an update can mix old and new page parts that don't work together.

What success looks like

  • The Settings page shows your settings and saves changes without this message.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who installed SMTO, mentioning any recent update. The installation may be incomplete. Don't delete SMTO's data to fix this; the problem is in the page files, not your data.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • settings.js could not find the shared window.SMTOAgentUi.apiJson client (agent_ui_shared.js did not load or is from an incompatible build), so Settings cannot make its server requests.

What this means

  • Settings initialization cannot find the shared UI apiJson component. This presentation or validation result does not establish an external task outcome. Use the saved run, resource revision and receipts when deciding whether an action can safely be repeated.

Why this can happen

  • Settings initialization cannot find the shared UI apiJson component.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect static asset loading and the expected shared component before changing settings.

How to fix it

  • settings.js apiJson() throws ui_shared_component_unavailable when window.SMTOAgentUi.apiJson is missing. Check the browser console and network tab for a failed /agent-ui/static/agent_ui_shared.js request, confirm the static files and the Server come from the same installed build, and reinstall or restart if the asset is missing or stale.
  • Reload the page after restoring access to its static assets. If it repeats, check that the installed UI and server come from the same build.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • Matching installed assets expose the required shared API helper.

What not to do

  • Do not remove retained state or weaken trust checks to make an unavailable dependency appear healthy.

Technical notes

  • This presentation or validation result does not establish an external task outcome. Use the saved run, resource revision and receipts when deciding whether an action can safely be repeated.
